correctness.rationale: The Jacobi beta moments E[X^2]=1/(2r+1), E[X^4]=3/[(2r+1)(2r+3)] give the projected jump derivative K(1-t^2)^r(1+(2r+3)tx). The total variation of that affine derivative is K(1-s^2)^r(2 if ks<=1 else ks+1/(ks)); the positive maximum solves the displayed quartic in s^2. Off-center dominance and the endpoint limits rule out the central/edge alternatives. A BV Stieltjes signed-jump representation extends the sharp step supremum to all BV inputs with equality at the two reflected one-jump steps. Independently evaluated the closed-form norm for r=.5,1,3,10,1000, obtaining 1.4439635015,1.6331820958,2.5628959010,5.9359582840,485.0304, consistent with the nonmonotonic and linear-concentration regimes. Proof requires the analytic quartic and BV reduction, not discrete grid tests.
